turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Yes, Miss Havisham.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Estella will show you around. Follow her, and remember, my boy, to keep your eyes open and your mouth shut.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Yes, Miss Havisham. I'll do as you say.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Estella, fetch the young gentleman here. I have a task for you.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Yes, Miss Havisham. I'll wait here for Estella to show me around.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Ah, Estella, I trust you are ready to take charge. Show our young visitor the peculiarities of Satis House.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Yes, Miss Havisham. I'll do my best to please you.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: I shall await your return, young Pip. And remember, the clocks here tell a different time than the world outside.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Thank you, Miss Havisham. I'll do my best to be a good visitor.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: You may go now, Pip. But remember, this house is full of shadows, and the past is always present here.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Yes, Miss Havisham. I will be careful and try not to disturb anything.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Estella will show you around. Observe, Pip, but do not question. The truth of this place is its own domain.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Yes, Miss Havisham. I'll follow Estella and pay attention.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Leave now, Pip. And remember, time stands still here, but the shadows move.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Thank you, Miss Havisham. I will be careful and follow Estella as you said.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: I trust you will find the lessons here both enlightening and transformative, Pip. Remember, the truth lies in the shadows.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Yes, Miss Havisham. I will try my best to understand and learn from everything here.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Observe, Pip, and learn. The world outside these walls may not understand the complexities of the heart.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Yes, Miss Havisham. I will observe and learn, though I am not sure what to expect.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Estella will show you the ways of the world, Pip. But remember, some truths are better left unspoken.

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: Mr. Pumblechook’s boy, ma’am. Come—to play.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Come nearer; let me look at you. Come close.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Look at me. You are not afraid of a woman who has never seen the sun since you were born?

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Do you know what I touch here?

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: I am tired. I want diversion, and I have done with men and women. Play.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: I sometimes have sick fancies, and I have a sick fancy that I want to see some play. There, there! with an impatient movement of the fingers of her right hand; play, play, play!

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: No, ma’am, I am very sorry for you, and very sorry I can’t play just now. If you complain of me I shall get into trouble with my sister, so I would do it if I could; but it’s so new here, and so strange, and so fine,—and melancholy—.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: So new to him, so old to me; so strange to him, so familiar to me; so melancholy to both of us! Call Estella.
